381508.literal_statement:
Let the pairs of graphs be those constructed in Figure 1 by adding horizontally symmetric planar graphs to the leftmost and rightmost vertices of the graph shown there. The resulting graphs have identical chromatic symmetric functions.

**Chromatic symmetric homology distinction conjecture.** Each such pair is distinguished by chromatic symmetric homology.

If true, this gives an infinite family of graph pairs that chromatic symmetric functions cannot distinguish but chromatic symmetric homology can. The claim is presented as conditional on the paper's earlier conjecture concerning the relevant graph automorphisms, so its resolution is not established here.

338226.title: Shur's Restivo–Salemi conjecture for power-free languages
338226.literal_statement: Let $\Sigma_k$ be a $k$-letter alphabet, and let $L_{k,\alpha}$ denote the language of $\alpha$-power-free finite words over $\Sigma_k$. For a language $L$, write ${\sf ext}(L)$ for its extendable factors. The language $L_{k,\alpha}$ has the **Restivo–Salemi property** when every pair of words $u,v\in {\sf ext}(L_{k,\alpha})$ can be joined by a word $w$ such that $uwv\in {\sf ext}(L_{k,\alpha})$. **Shur's Restivo–Salemi conjecture.** All power-free languages satisfy the Restivo–Salemi property. The property would imply that each power-free language has an infinite recurrent word whose subword complexity has the same growth rate as the language; the source attributes the conjecture to Shur and reports that it is based on extensive numerical studies, but gives no resolution.

338320.title: Fractal sum-product expansion conjecture
338320.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha,\beta,\delta \in (0,1)$. Assume that $A,B,E \subset [0,1]$ are compact sets with $\dim A \leq \alpha$, $\dim B \geq \beta$, and $\dim B + \dim E \geq \dim A + \delta$. **Fractal sum-product expansion conjecture.** There exists $t \in E$ such that

$$
\dim(A+tB) \geq \dim A+\epsilon
$$

for some $\epsilon>0$ depending only on $\alpha,\beta,\delta$. This conjecture is motivated by sum-product expansion phenomena and asks for a uniform dimension increase under addition by a suitable dilate; the supplied text does not state whether it is known or open.

338398.literal_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $C(n)$ be the family

$$
C(n):=\{abc:\ a+c\leq n,\ 2a+b\leq n,\ 1\leq a<b<c\leq n\}.
$$

A **domination conjecture for Turán hypergraphs.** If $H$ is a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $[n]$ such that every four vertices span an edge, then $H$ dominates $C(n)$. This conjecture is presented as a strengthening of Kalai's algebraic-shifting conjecture and would imply Turán's $(3,4)$-conjecture. No general resolution is given.

338401.title: Gedeon–Proudfoot–Young interlacing conjecture for matroid Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
338401.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid and let $e$ be an element of its ground set. Let $M/e$ be the contraction of $M$ at $e$. A matroid is **non-degenerate** if its rank is $0$ or its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial has degree $\left\lfloor \frac{\operatorname{rk} M-1}{2}\right\rfloor$. For real-rooted polynomials with positive leading coefficients, write $g(t)\preceq f(t)$ when the zeros interlace in the sense defined in the source. **Gedeon–Proudfoot–Young's conjecture.** If both $M$ and $M/e$ are non-degenerate, then

$$
P_{M/e}(t)\preceq P_M(t).
$$

The conjecture is known for uniform matroids of rank $n-1$ on $n$ elements and is proved in this paper for fan matroids; it remains open in general.

338484.title: Edel–Landjev–Xiang conjecture on the highest intersections with Hermitian surfaces
338484.literal_statement:
Let $V_2\subset\mathbb{P}^3(\mathbb{F}_{q^2})$ be a non-degenerate Hermitian surface, and let $F\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}[x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3]$ be homogeneous of degree $d$. Let $w_i$, for $1\leq i\leq 2d+1$, denote the $2d+1$ highest possible values of

$$
|V(F)\cap V_2|.
$$

**Edel–Landjev–Xiang conjecture.** For each $i$, there exist linear homogeneous polynomials $H_1,\ldots,H_d$ such that the hyperplanes $V(H_1),\ldots,V(H_d)$ contain a common line and

$$
|V(H_1\cdots H_d)\cap V_2|=w_i.
$$

The conjecture describes the extremal intersection values by unions of $d$ hyperplanes through a common line. It is stated here as a specialization of Conjecture 2(i) from the cited work, and no resolution is supplied in the text.

338576.title: The downer-vertex conjecture for chain graphs
338576.literal_statement:
A **chain graph** is a bipartite graph whose neighborhoods in each color class form a chain under inclusion. For a graph $G$, a vertex is **downer with respect to an eigenvalue** $\lambda$ if deleting that vertex decreases the multiplicity of $\lambda$.

**Downer-vertex conjecture.** In any chain graph, every vertex is downer with respect to every non-zero eigenvalue.

Non-zero eigenvalues of chain graphs are simple, so chain graphs have no Parter vertices for non-zero eigenvalues. The conjecture asserts that neutral vertices cannot occur for such eigenvalues.

338681.title: Espenschied's conjecture on complete multipartite graphs of polytopes
338681.literal_statement:
Let $K_{n_1,n_2,\dots, n_t}$ be the complete $t$-partite graph with part sizes $n_1,n_2,\dots,n_t$. If this graph is the graph of a polytope, then the set of its part sizes satisfies

$$
\\{n_1, n_2, \dots, n_t\\} \subset \\{1, 2\\}.
$$

**Espenschied's conjecture.** If $K_{n_1,n_2,\dots, n_t}$ is the graph of a polytope, then $\\{n_1, n_2, \dots n_t\\} \subset \\{1, 2\\}$ as sets. The classification of polytopes and combinatorial $3$-spheres with at most nine vertices provides applications to questions about which graphs can occur as the graphs of polytopes. The conjecture is attributed to Espenschied's work, but its resolution is not specified here.

338811.title: Monotonicity of strong geodetic number under the Cartesian product with $K_2$
338811.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $n(G)$ denote its order, and let $G \,\square\, K_2$ be the Cartesian product of $G$ with the complete graph on two vertices. Write $\operatorname{sg}(G)$ for the strong geodetic number of $G$. **Strong geodetic product conjecture.** If

$$
n(G)\geq 2,
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{sg}(G \,\square\, K_2) \geq \operatorname{sg}(G).
$$

338831.title: The composite-graph permitted motif conjecture
338831.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a composite graph with skeleton $\widehat G$. A **permitted motif** is a motif that supports a fixed point of the associated competitive threshold-linear network. Assume that $\widehat G$ is a permitted motif.

**Composite-graph permitted motif conjecture.** $G$ is a permitted motif if and only if every component $G_i$ is permitted.

This conjecture asks whether the characterization proved for disjoint, clique, and cyclic unions extends to all composite graphs whose skeletons are permitted motifs. The supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

338836.title: Keevash–Mubayi simplex-cluster strengthening conjecture
338836.literal_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$, and let a $d$-simplex-cluster be a $(d,k,2k)$-cluster that is also a $d$-simplex. A star is the family of all $k$-subsets containing a fixed element.

**Keevash–Mubayi strengthening conjecture.** For $d<k\le\frac{d}{d+1}n$, if $\mathcal{F}$ contains no $d$-simplex-cluster, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\le\binom{n-1}{k-1}.
$$

Equality holds only if $\mathcal{F}$ is a star. The source says this strengthens both the Erdős–Chvátal simplex conjecture and Mubayi's cluster conjecture, and does not state that it has been resolved.
